data.description:

data.title: China Aluminum International Engineering Names Liu Jing Chairman
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from China Aluminum International Engineering Corporation Limited Class H ( (HK:2068) ).

China Aluminum International Engineering Corporation Limited announced that Li Yihua will resign effective 27 November 2026 as chairman, executive director, member and chairman of the Strategy Committee, and authorised representative. He will leave all positions with the company; Li confirmed that he has no disagreement with the Board.

Effective the same date, executive director Liu Jing was elected chairman and Strategy Committee member and chairman, and appointed an authorised representative alongside executive director Tao Fulun. Liu also serves as the company’s general manager and deputy Party secretary, with his new term running concurrently with the fifth Board session.

data.title: Neo-Neon Enters Three-Year Framework Agreement with CNNC Hexin
data.description:

data.title: Maple Leaf Reports Lower Revenue and Profit for Year Ended August 2026
data.description:
China Maple Leaf Educational Systems ( (HK:1317) ) just unveiled an announcement.

China Maple Leaf Educational Systems Limited announced audited consolidated results for the year ended 31 August 2026. Revenue was RMB1,049.797 million, down 11.0% from the prior year, with PRC revenue falling 8.7% and overseas revenue declining 12.5%. Gross profit decreased 11.7% to RMB515.287 million.

Profit for the year fell 60.8% to RMB121.012 million, while basic earnings per share declined 59.5% to 4.27 RMB cents. EBITDA decreased 42.2% to RMB398.538 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell 21.6% to RMB374.789 million; the reconciliation identified non-recurring items including a RMB544.014 million gain on derecognition of certain payables and a RMB520.000 million goodwill impairment loss.

data.title: Macau Legend Proposes Share Consolidation, Board-Lot Change and Bye-Law Amendments
data.description:
An update from Macau Legend Development ( (HK:1680) ) is now available.

Macau Legend Development proposed consolidating every 10 existing shares into one consolidated share, which would reduce its issued shares from 930,178,068 to 93,017,806, assuming no further issuance or buybacks before effectiveness. Its authorised share capital would remain HK$1 billion, divided into 10 billion consolidated shares of HK$0.10 each.

The company also proposed changing the trading board lot from 4,000 existing shares to 5,000 consolidated shares, and amending and restating its bye-laws to align with legal and regulatory requirements under Hong Kong’s uncertificated securities market regime. Shareholder approval at a special general meeting is required, while circular dispatch is expected by 3 December 2026; the consolidation may not proceed.

data.title: Kowloon Development Agrees to HK$585 Million Rideon Disposal
data.description:
An update from Kowloon Development Co ( (HK:0034) ) is now available.

Kowloon Development Company Limited announced that its wholly owned subsidiary agreed on 27 November 2026 to sell 40% of Rideon Limited and assign its related sale loan to a purchaser for HK$585 million. The consideration comprises HK$1 for the shares and HK$584,999,999 for the loan, which was HK$800,632,953 as of 30 September 2026; 10% was payable on signing and the balance on completion.

Upon completion, the vendor will cease to own shares in Rideon. The transaction is discloseable because the applicable percentage ratio exceeds 5% but is below 25%, requiring reporting and announcement while remaining exempt from circular and shareholder approval requirements.

data.title: China Railway Signal & Communication Reports 14 Rail Transit Project Awards
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from China Railway Signal & Communication ( (HK:3969) ).

China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited said it was awarded 14 important projects from September to October 2026, including 11 railway projects and three urban rail transit projects. Railway awards included the RMB1.299 billion Jincheng special railway project, Mexico City’s AIFA-PACHUCA railway project at MXN1.37 billion, approximately RMB507 million, and projects involving the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, 350 km/h Fuxing EMUs and a Kazakhstan railway.

The urban rail awards cover communication, signaling, monitoring, access control, fire systems, fare collection and platform screen doors for extensions or upgrades involving Shanghai Metro Lines 12 and 19 and Dongguan Rail Transit Line 2. The disclosed projects span domestic and overseas markets and include EPC-plus-operation, electrification, train-control, onboard equipment and integrated urban rail systems work.
